newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses mixed, hit by inflation jitters.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses mixed, hit by inflation jitters.

text.p: European stocks got off to a mixed start on Wednesday with Wall Street's overnight return to a record-breaking pace counter-balanced by the re-emergence of inflation worries.

On currency markets, the dollar was slightly weaker in early trading after Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said Japan's economic recovery appeared to be becoming solid and industrial output was on an upward trend.

Frankfurt made the best start, boosted by New York's 40th record close of the year at 6,397.60 points. German Stocks climbed by 0.6 percent, but London and Paris were down with investors jittery over inflationary pressures.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, slipped 0.23 percent as the market took fright at British retail sales figures showing a rise of 0.4 percent in October, compared with a fall of 0.3 percent the previous month.

"Wall Street was nice, of course, but the market is in a bit of a quandary with the (British) political situation, next week's budget, rates and inflation worries and retail sales this morning. So it's looking a bit wobbly," one dealer said.
Investors were trying to assess the impact of the sales data on the prospects for interest rates and next Tuesday's budget.

Among stocks in the news, Eurotunnel was down 1-1/2p at 85p as investors fretted over the impact of this week's Channel Tunnel fire. Ferry operator P&O slipped also as the Financial Times Lex column warned investors the company might not benefit substantially from Eurotunnel's woes.

In Frankfurt, shares climbed strongly because of the Wall Street surge but lost some of the gains after a jump in the October business climate index measured by Germany's Ifo think-tank undermined lingering hopes of an interest rate cut.
The respected economics institute said its October survey showed a higher-than-expected jump in the business climate index last month to 97.4 percent from 95.7.
"The Ifo index was more or less stable but now there is a decent improvement," said one trader, adding that this had eroded hopes of a rate cut.
The figures pushed the computerised IBIS index into the minus column, but floor trading was holding up well by mid-morning.
In Paris, French stocks gave up initial gains as bond prices fell on the German Ifo survey, which revived inflation worries.

The dollar was weaker but off its lows against the yen caused by Matsushita's comments after Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka tempered the yen bullishness by saying he believed long-term rates were reflecting economic fundamentals.

Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International, said the yen was sensitive in Europe to a number of comments by Japanese officials, starting with those saying the bond market rally had been overdone.
"Then there were comments by Bank of Japan governor Matsushita that the economic recovery appeared to be more solid and finally Japan's finance minister debunking earlier comments," said Edmonds.

Against the mark, the dollar was weaker after the German business survey. "I am a bit surprised by the strength of this number. Hopes for a further rate cut (right now) will fade away," Guenter Redeker at Chase Manhattan in London said.
Currency traders later switched attention to U.S. September trade figures due out at 1330 GMT for clues to the health of the American economy.
CURRENCIES AT 1115 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.23 yen and 1.5008 marks, compared with 111.55 yen and 1.5036 marks in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1115 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 11 points at 3,967.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 0.11 points at 2,239.94.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 19.59 points at 2,783.74.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed $378.60 an ounce, compared to Tuesday's close of $378.45. Silver was at $4.90, up one cent.
